newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
ISOTIMIA

-- Officials of state oil company DEP-EKY estimate the oil deposits to be prospected in western Greece at around two milion barrels. Over the next six years, prospecting in the area will necessitate investments of some $100 million by a consortium of foreign oil companies and DEP-EKY which recently received a licence from the state.
-- A study of the relationship between interest rates and corporate profits stretching back seven years points to rising stock prices.
SUNDAY VIMA

-- Transportation minister Harry Kastanides revealed in an interview with the newspaper that Olympic Catering will be the ministry's next entity to seek a listing on the Athens bourse following OTE telecom.
-- Strong half-year profit growth of banks is attributed to portfolio gains from transactions in stocks and long-dated bonds, as well as to large interest spreads in consumer credit products.
SUNDAY ELEFTHEROTYPIA

-- The prime minister approved a widespread privatisation programme which calls for the sale of stakes in ten profitable public utilities and companies, starting with DEP, the oil refinery, and ending with the Public Power Corporation (PPC) beyond the year 2000.
KATHIMERINI
-- The government contemplates the full restructuring of PPC, currently a monopoly, to help it adjust to new conditions of competition when the market is opened up in 2001.

-- The development ministry is soon expected to announce a tender for the supply of hardware and software which will be used to set up a management information system for the areas of incorporated companies, insurance firms and state supplies. The system is budgeted at 0.57 billion drachmas.
SUNDAY KATHIMERINI

-- The Greek government is forced to reduce its taxation by up to 50 percent on used cars imported from the European Union (EU). The European Court has already dropped Greece's case for exemption from EU regulations and a final court ruling is due in in September 1997.

-- Banking rates are at a critical point due to a resurgence in consumer price inflation and short-term interbank rates. But the ministry of national economy sees scope for further banking rate cuts in view of lower treasury paper rates in coming months and steeper deceleration of inflation in 1998.
IMERISIA

-- Half-year banking profitability lifted the Athens stock exchange's benchmark index above 1,600 points amidst increased turnover. Analysts said stock prices respond to expectations of higher profitability and the rising dollar and see scope for appreciation in stocks with significant profit growth.

-- The finance ministry kept the rate unchanged at 9.60 percent on seven-year floating rate notes to be issued on July 29, seeking to raise 125 billion drachmas. The ministry also proceeds with the conversion of outstanding treasury stock into book-entry format.
KERDOS

-- The government will slash taxation on heating oil before October 1997 when heating oil price re-enters the basket of goods used for consumer price inflation calculations in an effort to pin inflation down.

-- Interbank rates eased below 12 percent following the cut in the Bank of Greece's basic and floor rates and the market expects further moves contriuting to even lower rates. The central bank sees room for a slight drop in interest rates following the boost in the system's liquidity.
NAFTEMBORIKI
-- Industrial output registered a 3.0 percent drop year-on-year in May 1997 according to figures released by the National Statistics Service.

-- The PPC will be converted into a holding company of two or three subsidiaries, one of which will be responsible for its distribution grid, as part of the government's restructuring plan ahead of market liberalisation in 2001.
EXPRESS
-- Strong buying interest for blue chip banks and industrial stocks led the Athens bourse's general index above 1,600 points.

-- Senior finance ministry officials told the financial press that upbeat interim profitability of banks cannot not be used as an excuse for imposing one-off, exceptional taxation. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
